steps.text: Thirty minutes earlier...
Underground structure, Highbury Borough, Londinium

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: You're back. How are things up top?

steps.name: Londinium Worker B
steps.text: Same as ever. Maybe worse.

steps.name: Londinium Worker B
steps.text: I used to be scared of those devil mercenaries who ask you for a smoke. The worst you'll get is a slap on the face if they feel like it.

steps.name: Londinium Worker B
steps.text: But now? It's all monsters you can't even describe that'll turn you into a puddle of blood without so much as blinking.

steps.name: Londinium Worker B
steps.text: You know what? I've been sleeping better. Because I know there's nothing but death if I run into one of them.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Are the Sarkaz still grabbing workers off the streets?

steps.name: Londinium Worker B
steps.text: Didn't see anything. We didn't dare go too far. Doesn't seem like the Sarkaz are interested in running the city anymore. There's no one maintaining public order.

steps.name: Londinium Worker B
steps.text: They couldn't fully occupy Londinium, could they? What use is it to them? Are they really planning to drive the Victorian capital all the way back to Kazdel?

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Who knows? Honestly, I haven't a clue what they're trying to do. Why go through so much trouble if they just want to kill everyone?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: How sad. Those who betrayed their friends for a better future are soon betrayed by the better future.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: No one expected things to turn out like this. You know we didn't mean to...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Let me guess—you mean us no harm but handed us to the Defense Forces out of fear. How kind and gentle. You all deserve a medal.

steps.name: Londinium Worker B
steps.text: Catherine, we...

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Save it. I don't have time to dig up old grudges, not that it would help anything anyway. At least you didn't gift wrap my head and Feist's and give them to the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: The question is, what do we do now?

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: We can hide here. We know the underground passages better than the Sarkaz—

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: That's your plan, Tommy? Live underground for the rest of your life like a talpibeast? Why don't you just go hide in a coffin, then?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I don't blame you for what you did. Given a choice, no one wants to go to war. But war is here now, right here in our homes.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: There's nowhere to run.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: I ran into a few fellows who said they could get us some decent weapons. I reckon—

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Is that thunder?

steps.name: Londinium Worker B
steps.text: Rain would be really nice right now.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: Why is it shaking? Is Londinium on the move?

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: But the mobility level is—

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Something's not right.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Let's head up and see what's happening. Be careful.

steps.name: Londinium Worker A
steps.text: What is it, Catherine? You're blocking the window.
The massive silhouette of The Shard is just visible from here.
The most familiar sight and the pride of all who call Londinium home.
But the annoying yet comforting blankets of clouds above are nowhere to be seen.

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Wait... What's that on top of the Shard?

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Take all our supplies and contact everyone we can. We need to move deeper underground now!

steps.name: Catherine
steps.text: Hurry!
Fifteen minutes earlier...
Silverrock Bluffs, Londinium Outskirts

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: We're approaching Silverrock Bluffs... That means the attacks will start soon.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: When I first heard Wellington's plan a few days ago...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Do you know what my initial reaction was?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: You thought it was too ambitious, your Grace?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Ambitious? I think you mean crazy.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Yes... crazy. He wants the entire allied forces committed to the front lines — thirteen dreadnoughts, forty-five assault ships, one hundred seventy-two gunboats...

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Eighty-six transports, ten support ships, all our artillery, and one hundred eighty thousand infantry, including the entire reserves.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: It wasn't an inquiry or request. It was a notice, almost an order.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Duke of Wellington has also abandoned the traditional Gaulish formation of multiple battle lines, instead having all fleets form single files to penetrate the Nachzehrer line all at once.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Gododdin and our forces are to be responsible for fire support and clearing out casters in the Sarkaz rear, while Wellington's vanguard charges at the center of the Nachzehrer formation.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Silverrock Bluffs, currently under Sarkaz control, is a key pass between the Redmane Mountains and the Duskglow River, and a highly defensible position.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The enemy can easily retreat towards Londinium, even if we win the battle.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: I would have staunchly opposed the plan, if it was not Wellington who proposed it.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: But you and the rest of the high commanders eventually consented to it.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: We've seen similar tactics in the military academies. They were the same tactics used in that legendary battle of the War of the Four Nations, in which Duke Wellington fought.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Victoria and Leithanien alliance split the Gaulish lines into three and quashed their resistance.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: That battle put Victorian on a new course for the next several decades.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Glorious as it may be, the past is no place to find refuge in.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Do you also think the Iron Duke has grown old?

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Wellington is a military genius.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: He commands battleships with the same ease and grace as a Leithanian virtuoso. I have never seen anyone quite like him.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: He is not one of those fools blindly chasing the glory of the past.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: The Sarkaz is not the end, but merely the beginning of the end of the real battle.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: As for here and now...

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: It's not just Wellington who needs a decisive victory.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Sarkaz have the Shard, and they have successfully fired it before. They could attack us or anywhere in Victoria at any moment.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: However, our war scholars deem any losses from Sarkaz Catastrophe attacks to be within acceptable limits.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Those losses will not compromise our ability to achieve our strategic objective.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Sarkaz have not refueled Londinium since it deviated from course. The city is immobile as of now.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Once we take the pass at Silverrock Bluffs, the Sarkaz will no longer have a terrain advantage, and the allied fleets will have a clear path to Londinium.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Indeed, if everything goes well–

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: We will be able to end this meaningless stalemate as quickly as possible.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Yet the word 'stalemate' isn't an apt description for the Sarkaz and Victoria.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Telegrams from the Caster hold are increasingly impatient. One cannot fault our backers for it. War is far too expensive.

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: A promise fulfilled too late is a promise unfulfilled.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Are those the cannons of Gastrell going off?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: The Duke of Wellington's attack has begun? But it's not time yet.

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: Your Grace, what's that red light coming from the distance?

steps.name: Flag Officer
steps.text: That light! It's coming from the top of the Shard!

steps.name: Duke of Caster
steps.text: Hail Wellington right now! We must—

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor! Are you okay?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The Doctor will be fine. Mon3tr absorbed the brunt of the impact.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The good news is that we fell into a canyon. Our precise location is uncertain, but we're at least a distance from the worst of the fighting.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Closure, Horn, and Siege have gone out to scout our surroundings. You should be briefed on the specifics soon.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: We're still assessing our personnel and equipment losses. Preliminary reports indicate that pre-impact measures were effective and losses are acceptable. Medical and engineering units are already at work.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm afraid there's been some troubling development.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Watch your step and keep up with us, Doctor.
Suffering extends its reach to every corner the eye can see.
From the top of the Shard, Originium spreads like a plague, devouring... assimilating.
Buildings, ships, armies... Originium devours all and quickly expands.
An unprecedented calamity indeed, one that puts even the most terrifying Catastrophes to shame.
And yet, an army marches through the roiling Originium crystals, its tattered banner visible even from here.
Suffering is but a marching order for the Sarkaz.
The ever-hungry procession of Sarkaz advances to the horns of wailing...
Sinking their teeth and claws into any enemy they find.
Blood-stained boulders litter the wasteland as far as the eye can see, looking decidedly out of place.
The whipping winds have ceased, giving way to a rising fog.
The withered grass remains unstirred, yet countless tattered bandages already dangle across.
Sarkaz warriors stand in line, soundless and motionless.
Waiting for the embodiment of death and decay, the master of war, their king.
A withered figure emerges from the death-filled fog.

a.text: Out of the fog, he glides, through wind and sand, rising from the withered grass.
And upon the Arts ritual circle he descends.
Tattered stripes of cloth fall to the blood-filled columns, like a bony hand caressing a tombstone.
Only the most seasoned warriors recognize that the Nachzehrer's tattered ribbons, like the banners on Kazdel's walls, belong to generations of ancient Sarkaz tribes.
Their form ragged, their symbols recognizable, but their scent of war unmistakable.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Duq'arael, Regent's Crimson, Prince of Blood.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: We were never close.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: But the contribution that you and your blood made to the war is undeniable.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: I bear witness to your glory and shame.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Slayer of the Feranmut in the Mist, Jailer of Time.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Usurper of the Royal Court, Executioner of Kings.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: You denied the path that we now walk, as you've denied the meaning of the Black Crown—

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: But you gave your first and final drop of blood to the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Your power shall not fade away, nor shall your anger, your hatred, your ambition.
He spreads his arms wide.
A black fog of decay rises, swallowing every boulder.
Red fades into sand and dirt, vanishing into the mist.
The warriors do not speak, but the earth begins to rumble as ancient witchcraft spreads across the battlefield.

a.text: 'War, we nourish you with our best.'
'Their blood and bones at your behest'
'We are the living and the dead.'
A drop of blood forms at the tip of Nezzsalem's staff.
It is the purest blood, the only blood that death and decay cannot touch.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: ...This is the Blood of Teekaz.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: It evoked the call of Amnannam, but was lost in the battle's Arts Circles. The Confessarii searched seventy of them without finding it.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: But Nezzsalem, Your Highness, you have found it for the Regent.
The drop of red liquid drifts toward Salus and enters her wrist.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Keep it safe, Confessarius.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Of course. I vow to protect it with all the strength of my bloodline... my life.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: The Vampiric Arts Circles are still active...

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: What of the Sanguinarch of Vampires? The purest bloodline, the cruelest of the sovereigns, the pride of the Sarkaz.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Did he really die so easily? At the hands of the young Banshee and the rabbit?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: He has not joined the myriad souls, but away has he drifted.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: What a shame to waste so much blood.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Meddler of bloodlines. Do not desecrate war and death with your flippant insolence.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Um...

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Apologies, your Highness, I was merely lamenting the loss of the Sanguinarch.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Then keep his legacy safe.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: His blood will continue the fight with us.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Of that, I have no doubt, Sovereign of the Withered Court.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: The Blood of Teekaz will fulfill its duty. If a mere tremble of Amnannam is enough to burn the heaven red and bring upheaval to the earth...

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Then its final descent shall free our fate from the manipulation of Originium, as the myriad souls have so longed for.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Fate?

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: War will crush all obstacles beneath its heel, even fate.
The Deadwood Throne rises, attended by innumerable war altars, casting a massive shadow on the battlefield.
Silent columns of warriors step into the strange Catastrophe, continuing their advance.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: We will advance before the storm.

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: Both the living and the dead—

steps.name: Nezzsalem
steps.text: This war belongs to all Sarkaz.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: A new beginning.

steps.name: Young Officer
steps.text: Another quote from one of the sovereigns, general?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I was simply reminded of the furnace at the center of Kazdel.

steps.name: Young Officer
steps.text: Oh, the big one. I witnessed many feedings before I came to Londinium.

steps.name: Young Officer
steps.text: It is an honor for a fallen warrior to be fed into it, becoming the fire that propels our progress.

steps.name: Young Officer
steps.text: But it never seems to be sated. Small wonder. The flames of a revenant's rage only burn stronger.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Nadine... would you call the nomadic city by the name of Kazdel your home?

spans.text: Nadine... would you call the nomadic city by the name of Kazdel your

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: What is the meaning behind the question, sir, when the final battle has already begun?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: I was raised on the battlefields outside Kazdel. The black rocks and the bones of my fellow Nachzehrer are the only things buried beneath the city's walls and wheels.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: Where is home, if not Kazdel?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Yes... What other answer could there be?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The future is lined with uncertainties, but this much we know: this war ends where a new beginning emerges.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Have you made contact with Ulšulah?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: No. They were very thorough in mopping up Brentwood.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: Just as you predicted, our casters have picked up the trail of the Feranmut skeleton's movement. They considered attacking Londinium... attacking The Shard directly.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I gave them a chance... far too many chances.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: There is no question that Major Ulšulah has been negligent in her duty. She had better have a good explanation... if she lives to explain.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Have you located the skeleton?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: We have a rough idea of its location, but it will take time to find it on this vast battlefield. Should I take a squad there personally?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No. I will.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: We will retake the Feranmut's spine, or destroy it. It must not fall into the wrong hands again.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: You're going yourself?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Those mercenaries have interfered too much. They must be eliminated.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Before that, though... we will finish the ritual.

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: Our Nachzehrer ritual? I didn't think you cared much for tradition.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Cyclops, Lich, Wendigo, Banshee... more and more have left.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You've never seen these Royal Courts in Kazdel, have you, young Nachzehrer?

steps.name: Nadine
steps.text: I suppose not. Other than the Nachzehrer, it's mostly been Vampires. Not the best neighbors, but you start to miss their smell when you spend enough time in Londinium.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: The blood of the fallen has returned to the earth.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: There will be no new Prince of the Crimson Court.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: How many sovereigns do the Sarkaz have left?
'Bzzzz—'
'Logistics to Command. We've encountered a Catastrophe near Sufrior Chasm.'
'At least, I think it's a Catastrophe... we're being drowned in a tide of Originium.'
'The ship has lost power. Weapon systems severely damaged... all systems inoperative!'
'Defense systems offline... no response from Arts unit... I repeat, all systems inoperative...'
'Enemy spotted! Taking heavy fire, mobile Arts device... *Bzzt*...'
'Data... automatic record...'

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: None of these messages made it out.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The entire communications system is scrap. To think that so many have died to protect this little metal box...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: ...I salute you.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Phew... that bow hurt. I shouldn't take my hat off...

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Our foe is unpredictable, aren't they? There's enough intel about The Shard to fill an entire building.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: But you and I must take the blame for our present circumstances.
The man in a hat looks down at his counterpart.
The man on the ground lies motionless, buried to his chest in crystal-filled dirt. But the little box that he clutches in his left hand remains spotless.
The Trilby Asher pulls the rim of his fallen comrade's hat down, covering the face that no one knew to begin with.
It took a little more effort to retrieve the communicator, but war has made him a rather proficient undertaker.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Intel retrieved.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Communications are still being jammed by severe interference.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: A little progress is better than nothing, I suppose.
'The Duke of Fife and the Sixth Infantry Battalion were ambushed. The landing attempt on the Crumley plate has failed.'
'Unable to reach the Duke of Gododdin's scout fleet. Chetleigh has been lost.'
'Large-scale unanticipated geological changes across the Silverrock Bluffs front. Active Originium concentration above threshold.'

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: No good news.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Are those... troops?

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: The ID code is—

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: My, my... what a miracle. I am a lucky man indeed.

steps.name: 'Trilby Asher'
steps.text: Hm?
